record.paper_title: Recent advances and open questions on the susy structure of the chiral de Rham Complex
record.context_brief: Spin(7) elliptic genus as topological-twist graded dimension
record.original_question: For a Spin(7)-holonomy manifold M, is its elliptic genus equal to the graded dimension of the BRST/topological-twist cohomology H(C∞(M, Ω_ch(M)), Q−_0) constructed from the conjectural left-moving SV^Spin7 structure, with finite-dimensional conformal-weight spaces?

evidence.quote: Assuming that we have two commuting copies of SV Spin7 inside of C∞(M, ΩchM ) we want to obtain the elliptic genus of M as some form of graded dimension of this vertex algebra.

Conjecturally one would obtain a vertex algebra such that its graded dimension: trH(ΩchM ,Q−0 ) qL+0 −c/24, coincides with the elliptic genus of M, in particular, it should have finite dimensional conformal weight spaces.
2 Question. Is the elliptic genus of a Spin7 manifold M the graded dimension of the topological twist H(C∞(M, ΩchM ), Q−0 ) described in 4.22?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact Riemannian manifold of dimension 8 with holonomy group equal to $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$. Let $\Omega^{ch}_M$ denote the chiral de Rham complex of $M$ (the sheaf of vertex superalgebras introduced by Malikov–Schechtman–Vaintrob), and let $C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M)$ denote its space of global smooth sections, viewed as a vertex superalgebra equipped with the natural conformal grading by $L_0$ and central charge $c=12$.

Assume that $C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M)$ contains two commuting copies of the Shatashvili–Vafa $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$ vertex superalgebra $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$, one for each chirality. From the left-moving copy, let $Q^-_0$ denote the BRST/topological-twist differential associated with the topological twist of this $\mathcal{SV}^{\mathrm{Spin}(7)}$ structure, and form the cohomology
$$H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),\,Q^-_0).$$
This cohomology inherits a grading by the conformal weight $L_0$ (and possibly by an additional fermion-number/$U(1)$-type charge needed to define the elliptic genus).

Question: Are the conformal-weight homogeneous components of $H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),Q^-_0)$ all finite-dimensional, and does its graded dimension
$$\mathrm{tr}_{H(C^\infty(M,\Omega^{ch}_M),Q^-_0)}\,q^{L_0-c/24}$$
(suitably refined by the available charge to a two-variable trace) coincide with the elliptic genus of the $\mathrm{Spin}(7)$-manifold $M$?
artifact.category_tag: Chiral de Rham complex and elliptic genera
artifact.status_search_result: No proof of the conjectural identification of the Spin(7) elliptic genus with the graded dimension of the topological-twist cohomology of the chiral de Rham complex (via the Shatashvili–Vafa Spin(7) vertex superalgebra) appears in the literature. Related works study CDR topological twists, decompositions of Spin(7) elliptic genera via mock-modular characters, and the embedding of $\mathcal{SV}^{Spin(7)}$, but the question itself is stated as a conjecture/open problem and no resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: On the Elliptic Genera of Manifolds of Spin(7) Holonomy
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses decomposition of the Spin(7) elliptic genus via conjectured characters (mock modular forms) but does not establish the CDR/topological-twist identification.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on Spin(7) elliptic genera does not prove the conjectural CDR graded-dimension identification.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Calabi–Yau manifolds and the chiral de Rham complex
status_evidence.snippet: Studies N=2 structures and topological twists on the chiral de Rham complex but does not resolve the Spin(7) case.
status_evidence.claim: Topological twists of CDR are studied in adjacent settings; the Spin(7) statement remains conjectural.
